observations.semantic_recognizability: v006 reads as a tall tool cupboard in the Room B review render.
observations.silhouette_quality: The crown and plinth retain a wardrobe silhouette, but the two narrow, almost closed door slabs do not match the target’s broad open doors.
observations.proportion: Godot measures 42 x 69.9 x 27.88 inches; source depth exceeds the authoritative 22-inch envelope by 5.88 inches.
observations.geometric_detail: Shelves, a small tool rack and a lower drawer are present, but the render leaves most of the cabinet empty and the door faces lack readable panel construction.
observations.material_realism: The oak/walnut distinction is present, though all wood reads as smooth and uniformly lit.
observations.surface_variation: The production render shows minimal visible grain variation across doors, carcass and shelves.
observations.close_up_quality: The detail render shows broad plain faces and sparse tool silhouettes; the approved target has richly fitted tools, panels, rails and hardware.
observations.gameplay_readability: The tall cabinet remains identifiable in the Room B scene.
observations.scale_fidelity: The source depth is 27.88 inches against the RoomDefinition’s 22 inches, so the candidate fails exact proportion fidelity.
observations.art_direction_fit: The closed-looking doors and sparse tool bay diverge materially from the approved open tool-wardrobe concept.
observations.technical_integration: Godot imports the GLB, but technical validation fails because the source proportions exceed tolerance; the diagnostic render does not change that status.

hard_fail_reasons: Technical validation fails: source depth is 27.88 inches versus the authoritative 22-inch depth.
The target’s broad open doors and densely fitted tool bay are not transferred.
defects: Door rotation and width leave the cabinet looking nearly closed.
The center tool bay is sparse and most wood members have a uniform finish.
next_action_hypothesis: Bake each door rotation into its mesh before material merging, update Blender bounds after transforms, and validate the exported GLB. Open the broad doors toward the cabinet sides within the 22-inch depth, then fill the tool bay with legible fitted tools and stronger wood grain.
incumbent_comparison: Compared with room_tool_wardrobe-v005, room_tool_wardrobe-v006 is a useful challenger but does not clear the target’s strict transfer gate. The source proportion defect and visible detail loss keep the incumbent as the safer current review choice.

thickness.evidence: The diagnostic views show plausible thickness in the cabinet sides and top, but the saved technical validation still fails because the GLB exceeds the exact 42 x 70 x 22-inch envelope.

hardware.evidence: The nearly closed wardrobe doors conceal most of the tool bay, and the visible small pulls do not provide the target’s readable hinge and fitted hardware treatment.

material_response.evidence: Room_tool_wardrobe v006 uses separated wood tones, but the large door and side planes render uniformly with little finished timber response.

surface_variation.evidence: The registered diagnostic detail of room_tool_wardrobe v006 shows almost no board-to-board grain or wear variation.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The tool bay in room_tool_wardrobe v006 appears sparse and the doors nearly closed, so the visible construction falls well short of the approved fitted workshop wardrobe.
